-74.39600,40.54120.name: Center for Advanced Reproductive Medicine & Fertility
-74.39600,40.54120.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Suna M. Qasim, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-121.75400,38.53800.name: Mutant Mouse Resource & Research Centers

It is also a permanent archive of engineered animals maintained indefinitely, and the animals in it are excluded by statute from the count of animals used in US research.

-42.36670,-21.10000.name: Paraíba do Sul basin — recorded spread
-42.36670,-21.10000.state: Muriaé, Minas Gerais — headwater creeks of the Paraíba do Sul basin, Atlantic Forest
-42.36670,-21.10000.desc: The first engineered animal known to have established a self-sustaining population in the wild. Fluorescent zebrafish were found in all five sampled headwater creeks of the southeastern Paraíba do Sul basin, first seen in 2015, beside Latin America's largest ornamental aquaculture centre whose roughly 4,500 ponds discharge into those streams. Surveys since show them breeding year-round with a peak in the rainy season, and reaching maturity earlier than unmodified zebrafish, which speeds the cycle further. They are banned in Brazil and were still being advertised for sale there. A single specimen found in Florida canals in 2014 did not establish, most likely because something ate it; here there is no predator that takes them. Three things line up in one record: a ban that did not stop the sale, a pond wall that was the entire containment measure, and a trait that is visible to the naked eye — which is the only reason anyone noticed at all.
